Using a neural-network emulator (${\tt NNERO}$), we perform a MCMC analysis that combines late-time probes of the reionization history and galaxy UV luminosity functions. We find that including PMF energy losses significantly relaxes previous bounds, as the reduced field strength suppresses their imprint on observables. Employing a Fisher matrix analysis, we estimate the sensitivity of the 21$\,$cm signal experiment HERA to the PMFs' imprint on intergalactic medium perturbations and show that 21$\,$cm cosmology could significantly improve on current bounds, depending on assumptions on the astrophysics. Our results highlight the importance of modeling PMF evolution self-consistently with the IGM evolution to extract current bounds and future sensitivities.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.26022.title: Secondary Dependence of Baryonic Effects on the Density Profile of Dark Matter Halos
arxiv.org/abs/2604.26022.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.26022v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Baryonic physics is anticipated to be a major source of systematic uncertainty in current and future large-scale cosmological surveys. We investigate how baryonic effects on halo density profiles vary with secondary halo properties at fixed halo mass, using the large-volume MillenniumTNG hydrodynamical simulation and its dark matter-only counterpart. We focus on the impact of halo concentration and large-scale environment on the ratio of density profiles of matched halos in the hydrodynamical and dark matter-only simulations. At redshift $z = 0.0$, we find a strong dependence on halo concentration, especially at lower halo mass ($12.5 < \log(M_h/h^{-1}M_{\odot}) < 13.0$), where more concentrated halos exhibit weaker inner enhancement and stronger intermediate-radius suppression at fixed halo mass, with variations reaching $\sim 15\%$ at small scales and decreasing toward larger scales. This trend weakens and reverses at higher halo mass. In contrast, the secondary dependence on large-scale environment is weaker ($\sim 2\%$) and largely scale-independent, with halos in denser regions exhibiting slightly weaker intermediate suppression. By separating internal profile redistribution from total mass suppression, we show that concentration impacts both components, whereas the environmental dependence is primarily associated with an overall mass shift. These secondary dependencies persist at $ z = 0.5$ and correlate with variations in internal baryonic properties. We examine additional halo properties, including halo spin and velocity dispersion, and find significant secondary dependence. Overall, our results highlight the important role of secondary halo properties in modulating baryonic effects on halo density profiles, with potential implications for future modeling efforts.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.13982.title: Lyman-alpha Radiation Pressure in Dense Star Clusters: Implications for Star Formation and Winds at Cosmic Dawn
arxiv.org/abs/2605.13982.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.13982v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Observations with the JWST in lensed fields have revealed that galaxies at cosmic dawn may concentrate their star formation in highly dense, compact, star clusters. The high columns and low metallicities encountered in their birth environments suggest that Lyman-alpha (Ly$\alpha$) radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution. In this study, we address this question by post-processing snapshots from radiation hydrodynamic simulations of dense star cluster-forming clouds ($\Sigma_*\gtrsim10^3{M_\odot{pc}^{-2}}$) with a range of dust abundances ($Z_d=0-0.1Z_{d,\odot}$) using the COLT Monte Carlo code. We infer that Ly$\alpha$ is likely to have mild (~10%) effects on the gas-to-star conversion efficiencies ($\epsilon_*\gtrsim60$%) for $Z_d\gtrsim0.01Z_{d,\odot}$, and even in dust-free environments, $\epsilon_*\gtrsim25$% - much higher than the <10% values typical of star-forming regions in the local Universe. This is because the densest filaments dominating stellar mass assembly ($n\gtrsim10^4{cm}^{-3}$) remain sub-Eddington ($f_{Edd}<1$). On the other hand, the bulk of the gas volume ($n\lesssim10^3{cm}^{-3}$) has $f_{Edd}>1$, with noticeable fractions having $f_{Edd}\gtrsim10$, implying that Ly$\alpha$ can launch dynamically significant winds from these systems rapidly ($\lesssim$4Myr), with possible implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows. The Ly$\alpha$ force multiplier $M_F$ is highly sensitive to $Z_d$, with $M_F\lesssim3$ ($\lesssim 500$) for $0.1Z_{d,\odot}$ (dust-free) environments respectively. Nevertheless, Ly$\alpha$ dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all values of $Z_d\lesssim0.1Z_{d,\odot}$, by factors of ~3-500. Our results suggest that Ly$\alpha$ radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.21578.title: Gravitational wave detectability range informed by external messengers
arxiv.org/abs/2605.21578.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.21578v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A rapid estimate of gravitational-wave (GW) detectability associated with astronomical transients is crucial for optimizing multi-messenger follow-up strategies and for constraining the physical origin of the transient itself. We introduce here the Targeted Detectability Range (TDR), designed to evaluate, with minimal computational effort, the detectability of compact binary coalescences under the hypothesis of association with an external messenger, such as an electromagnetic or neutrino signal. Unlike the standard GW range, which is based on averaged source parameters, the TDR incorporates prior information from observations of the external messenger, including sky localization, inclination constraints, and physically motivated bounds on component masses. We report the TDR of all short- and long-duration gamma-ray bursts, observed during the first three observing runs of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo. The method is validated by performing a systematic comparison with the 90$\%$ exclusion distances provided by modeled targeted GW searches. In the absence of a coincident detection by all-sky, all-time GW searches, the TDR provides a rapid and quantitative constraint on a possible merger origin of the astrophysical source. Its low-latency implementation and public availability would enable timely prioritization of follow-up observations and optimized allocation of observational resources, with direct impact on the physical interpretation of astronomical transients.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.11322.title: Ring Position Angles and Spin in M87* and Sgr A*
arxiv.org/abs/2606.11322.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.11322v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) images of black holes appear as rings with a brightness asymmetry. Here, we expand on our previous study of the asymmetry magnitude $a_1$ to study the position angle of the peak brightness asymmetry $\mathrm{PA}_1$ in general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) models. For larger spin magnitudes ($a_{*}>0$ and $a_{*}\lesssim-0.5$), the mean $\mathrm{PA}_1$ falls within $1\sigma$ of the approaching limb of the black hole, regardless of viewing inclination, disk magnetization, or source. By comparing the $(a_1, \mathrm{PA}_1)$ distribution in M87* observations with models, we demonstrate that we can mildly disfavor low-magnitude spins and strongly disfavor all spin vectors that point toward Earth. The alignment of $\mathrm{PA}_1$ relative to the large-scale jet axis may suggest that M87*'s disk does not have a large tilt. By combining $\mathrm{PA}_1$ with the pattern speed measured in optimistic 2026 M87* video conditions, the EHT can constrain whether M87* is prograde or retrograde with $\sim 84\%$ accuracy. In Sgr A*, we show that a detection of $(a_1, \mathrm{PA}_1)$ could constrain the magnitude and direction of the galactic center spin vector. Finally, if future EHT expansions increase the sample of horizon-scale sources, a simple set of observables (ring diameter, asymmetry magnitude, and asymmetry angle) could enable robust constraints on black hole mass, spin, and inclination.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.30200.title: Cosmology with Intensity Mapping via Statistics Beyond the Power Spectrum in the SKAO Era
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30200.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30200v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The cosmological distribution of neutral hydrogen (HI) during the post-reionization era is highly non-Gaussian due to the underlying non-linear structure formation, complex galaxy biasing, and potential primordial non-Gaussianity. One needs higher-order (beyond two-point) statistics to maximally extract the non-Gaussian information out of the 21-cm intensity maps. This chapter summarizes the potential of several higher-order statistics, including voxel intensity distribution, emission line stacking, probability density functions, $\ell_1$-norm, bispectrum, and various marked statistics. Additionally, image-based morphological descriptors, such as the Largest Cluster Statistic, local dimensions, and Minkowski functionals, etc., can potentially characterize the morphology and geometry of the cosmic web encoded in the 21-cm intensity maps. This chapter presents forecasts of the detectability of these higher-order statistics in the context of the future SKAO observations. These forecasts incorporate instrumental noise, observational effects, and, in some cases, foreground removal in their analyses. With its unprecedented sensitivity, the future SKAO 21-cm observations will enable us to measure these higher-order statistics more precisely, possibly helping to break degeneracies between astrophysical and cosmological parameters, and maximizing the science outcome from these surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.01412.title: Fractional-Dimension Gravity and the Milky Way Galaxy
arxiv.org/abs/2607.01412.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.01412v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In this work, we focus our analysis of Fractional-Dimension Gravity (FDG) on our home galaxy, the Milky Way (MW), by using the latest Gaia DR3 data as well as previous rotation curve (RC) data for this galaxy. FDG is an alternative gravitational model (previously known as Newtonian Fractional-Dimension Gravity - NFDG) which does not require the dark matter (DM) paradigm.
  The MW is studied here with the methods of FDG and its observed rotation curves are successfully reproduced by using a variable fractional dimension $D\left (R\right)$, following previous studies of several other galaxies which were analyzed with the same methodology. An alternative dimension function $D_{m}\left(R \right)$, based on the mass-dimension field equation, was also used and yielded less accurate fits to the experimental data.
  In addition, we also considered possible implications of the FDG metric, based on the presence of additional weights, on the structure of Special Relativity (SR) for spacetimes with fractional dimension. One notable, but very speculative outcome of this analysis is the possibility of an effective superluminal motion in galactic regions where the space dimension is $D<3$.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.03514.title: Disentangling modified gravity and galaxy bias with field-level inference
arxiv.org/abs/2607.03514.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.03514v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a field-level inference framework for testing gravity with large-scale structure, exploiting the full information of the galaxy distribution. Traditional analyses based on the power spectrum discard non-Gaussian and Fourier phase information, resulting in strong degeneracies between modified gravity (MG) and galaxy bias. Our approach overcomes this limitation by performing a Bayesian analysis directly on the three-dimensional galaxy number counts, jointly constraining MG and bias parameters using both amplitudes and phases. As an illustrative application, we analyse mock data in real space in the context of $f(R)$ gravity and a non-linear galaxy bias model designed to mimic the real-data 2M++ BORG analysis of Jasche&Lavaux (2019). Non-linear structure formation is modelled using COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (COLA) under different gravity strengths, parameterised by $f_{R0}$. The resulting dark-matter fields are then mapped to mock galaxy catalogues via a non-linear bias prescription. We demonstrate that, with the initial phases assumed known, including non-Gaussian and phase information yields tighter constraints on both $f_{R0}$ and the primary bias parameter $\beta$ (corresponding to the linear galaxy bias on large scales), relative to power-spectrum-only analyses. Notably, the field-level approach breaks the degeneracies between MG and galaxy bias inherent to two-point statistics. Through a cosmic-web classification into voids, walls, filaments and clusters, we find that under-dense regions are the primary drivers in distinguishing gravity at the field level. Finally, we establish the robustness of our pipeline against variations in initial conditions, Poisson noise, and galaxy-field thresholding, providing a powerful path forward for field-level tests of gravity.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.07044.title: Revisiting 2D and 3D Dainotti Correlations for GRBs Using Bayesian Neural Networks
arxiv.org/abs/2608.07044.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.07044v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are promising cosmological probes, but their use as standard candles is limited by the circularity problem, necessitating model-independent calibration of GRB luminosity correlations. We revisit the two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) Dainotti correlations using Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) trained on the updated Observational Hubble Data (OHD) and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernova sample. The reconstructed luminosity distances are used to calibrate the Platinum and Narendra et al. GRB samples. We constrain the parameters of the 2D Dainotti relation and the 3D fundamental plane, and examine the impact of calibration datasets and GRB sample selection. Calibration achieved using Pantheon+ yields tighter constraints than OHD, while the 3D correlation exhibits lower intrinsic scatter than the 2D relation. Our results demonstrate that BNNs provide a robust framework for model independent calibration of GRB luminosity correlations with reliable uncertainty propagation. Further, the underlying distance probe is a key factor in model-independent calibration, determining both the size of the GRB samples and the precision of the resulting constraints.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.24998.title: Black hole astrometric binaries in the Roman Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey
arxiv.org/abs/2608.24998.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.24998v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Roman), NASA's next flagship mission, is currently scheduled to launch in August 2026. As part of its mission, Roman will conduct the Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS), which will generate $\sim$50,000 epochs of high-precision photometric and astrometric data for $\sim 10^8$ sources across 1.7 deg$^2$ in the Galactic Bulge. Roman GBTDS astrometry is comparable to Gaia Data Release 4 in terms of number of stars, astrometric precision, and time baseline, and is highly complementary in terms of wavelength and sky location. In this paper, we investigate a synthetic population of GBTDS sources to characterize the detectability of unresolved astrometric binaries, in particular those with compact object companions. Assuming the occurrence rate of black holes (BHs) and neutron stars (NSs) in AU-scale orbits around stars is $10^{-7}$ and $10^{-6}$, respectively, and that Roman achieves an astrometric precision of $1\%$ of a pixel, $\mathcal{O}(10)$ BH+star and $\mathcal{O}(10)$ NS+star detached binaries will be detectable. The BHs will have median mass measurement uncertainties of $\sim 25\%$, increasing the existing sample of detached astrometric BH binaries by a factor of three. Together with the $\mathcal{O}(10^2)$ isolated BHs expected to be discovered by microlensing in the Roman GBTDS and an additional $\mathcal{O}(10)$ detached BH binaries in Gaia DR4, this will provide a representative view of the quiescent Galactic stellar-mass BH population.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.28507.title: Relativistic outflows power a quasi-periodic eruption: constraints on energetics, mass loss, and emission mechanisms
arxiv.org/abs/2608.28507.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.28507v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are recurring bursts of X-ray radiation originating from supermassive black holes (SMBHs). They are an unprecedented type of structured, high-amplitude SMBH variability, but the physical origins of their regularity, timescales, energetics, and emission are uncertain. We present new XMM-Newton observations of the QPEs in ZTF19acnskyy/"Ansky", constituting the deepest observations of individual bursts in any source thus far. The X-ray spectra reveal time-evolving P Cygni profiles comprising blueshifted absorption and redshifted emission from L-shell transitions of Fe XIX-XXIV, with column densities $N_H\sim 10^{22-23}$ cm$^{-2}$ and bulk velocities of $|v_w/c|\sim 0.2$, indicating relativistic mass ejections during each eruption. We construct a time-dependent analytical model of a wind turning on to self-consistently compute its evolving luminosity and ionization properties, and find that the light curve and spectral lines can be simultaneously produced by a wide-angle outflow with $\dot{M}\sim 10^{-9}-10^{-8}\,M_\odot$ s$^{-1}$ kinetically powering the X-rays with an efficiency of $L_X/\dot{E}_K\sim 0.1$. For a covering fraction $f_\Omega\sim0.5$, each eruption ejects $\sim 10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ and $\gtrsim 10^{49}$ erg of kinetic energy, setting an upper bound on the QPE lifetime of $\lesssim1000$ bursts if the underlying mass reservoir is $\sim1 M_\odot$, and implying that the bursts may result in detectable multiwavelength signatures of reverberation and feedback. These measurements provide new quantitative constraints on QPE energetics, emission mechanisms, and the mass/energy they recycle into their circumnuclear environments, as well as an observational probe for direct comparison with physical models and hydrodynamical simulations of QPEs.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.19689.title: Probing submillimeter number counts below the confusion limit: extreme-value statistics of the P(D) distribution and its modulation by gravitational lensing
arxiv.org/abs/2609.19689.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.19689v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The shape of the submillimeter galaxy number counts below the confusion limit is a key record of cosmic star formation but is accessible only statistically, through the one-point distribution of map surface brightness, $P(D)$. Classical $P(D)$ analysis compresses the counts into flux-integrated constraints and requires a full instrument forward model. We introduce an extreme-value-theory analysis of the confusion $P(D)$ tail: the peaks-over-threshold formalism, in which exceedances above a threshold $u$ follow a generalized Pareto distribution (GPD). The GPD shape parameter $\xi(u)$ is a flux-resolved, normalization-free readout of the local logarithmic slope of the counts, and its gravitational-lensing modulation $\Delta\xi(u)$ probes their local curvature. We derive analytic relations for both, validate them with end-to-end simulations, and apply the method to Planck 857 GHz maps and the Herschel/SPIRE 350 $\mu$m map of GAMA-09. At Planck's 5' resolution the tail reflects the bright, clustered sky rather than the faint counts, though the background alone excludes the single power-law count model. At SPIRE resolution $\xi$ rises markedly with threshold, consistent with the strongly lensed bright population (a first detection of lensing in a $P(D)$ tail), and the bright-masked map favors the Schechter model. Behind galaxy clusters we set the first calibrated upper limits on $\Delta\xi(u)$. CCAT/FYST should separate the count models directly, but a cluster-lensing detection needs more $10^{15}\,M_\odot$ clusters than the sky contains. The GPD tail statistic thus discriminates the functional form of the counts at fluxes of order the threshold, below the detection limit, invariant to map mean, gain and count normalization, and robust to clustering; lensing supplies a calibrated ruler for count features, whose detection awaits deep, high-resolution surveys of massive clusters.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.29462.title: Limits on Primordial Black Hole Evaporation from LUX-ZEPLIN
arxiv.org/abs/2609.29462.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.29462v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) collaboration recently reported a singular anomalous nuclear recoil event at $248 \pm 23 \, \rm keV$, accompanied by a strict null result for unexplained excesses in their primary $5.4-50 \, \rm keV$ search window. The macroscopic momentum transfer required to generate this event is kinematically inaccessible to standard halo cold dark matter (CDM), naturally motivating models featuring light, relativistic relics. In this work, we investigate whether a contemporary flux of Hawking-boosted dark matter (DM) emitted by evaporating Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) in the $10^{11}-10^{13} \, \rm g $ mass range can source the anomaly. By parameterizing the nuclear scattering with heavy non-relativistic effective field theory (NREFT) operators and endothermic inelastic mass transitions, we formulate a strict kinematic exclusion. We demonstrate that the inherent thermal nature of the Hawking emission, coupled with the relativistic kinematics of the incident flux, inevitably overproduces low-energy recoils, aggressively violating the LZ background bounds. Utilizing this failure, we map the LZ low-energy null results into novel, highly stringent upper limits on the PBH abundance fraction, excluding $f_{\rm PBH} \gtrsim 10^{-6}$ for $M_{\rm PBH} \sim 2 \times 10^{11} \, \rm g $ at $ 90 \% $ confidence level.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.30382.title: Selective state space model for photon energy estimation in microwave kinetic inductance detectors
arxiv.org/abs/2609.30382.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.30382v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) are superconducting photon counting detectors that simultaneously measure the energy and arrival time of individual photons and are suitable for large-format arrays. The energy resolving power R = E/$\Delta$E is the primary figure of merit for spectrophotometric applications. It is limited in practice by the assumptions underlying the Wiener optimal filter used to estimate photon energy: stationary noise, linear response, and energy independent pulse shapes, all of which MKIDs structurally violate. We present Venom (Very Efficient Neural Optimal-filter for MKIDs), a selective state space model based on the Mamba architecture that replaces the coordinate transform and optimal filter, operating directly on raw in-phase/quadrature timestream data, carrying 3,314 trainable parameters, and targeting deployment on the MKIDGen3 and future system-on-chip readout platforms. To deal with the small calibration datasets typical of MKID experiments, we train on synthetic pulses drawn from a streaming principal component analysis that samples photon energy continuously between calibration wavelengths. All numbers are reported on a stratified 15% held-out validation set, with R measured from a kernel density estimate. On an InHf bilayer resonator (ten wavelengths, 254-1310nm), Venom reaches a mean R of 26.4 versus 24.2 for the published per-wavelength optimal filter baseline, a 9% improvement from one model in place of ten per-laser filter templates. The R of 38.6 at 254 nm is the highest ever recorded for an ultraviolet-to-near-infrared MKID suitable for use in a dense array. On a PtSi resonator (five wavelengths, 808-1310nm), where the published analysis used one shared 920nm template, Venom matches the optimal filter, with a mean R of 9.1 versus 8.8 at the three interior wavelengths.

arxiv.org/abs/2511.01325.title: U-spin symmetry energy and hyperon puzzle in $\Lambda$-admixed neutron stars
arxiv.org/abs/2511.01325.excerpt:
arXiv:2511.01325v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: By combining the ($u$,$d$) I-spin doublets or ($d$,$s$) U-spin doublets, the SU(3) flavor symmetry of light quarks can be decomposed into SU(2)$_I\times$U(1)$_Y$ or SU(2)$_U\times$U(1)$_Q$ subgroups, which have been widely adopted to categorize hadrons and their decay properties. The standard I-spin counterpart for the interactions among nucleons, namely the nuclear symmetry energy $E_\mathrm{sym}(n_\mathrm{b})$, characterizes the variation of binding energy as the neutron to proton ratio in a nuclear system. We propose the U-spin symmetry energy $E_\mathrm{U}(n_\mathrm{b})$ for hyperonic matter to characterize the variation of binding energy with the inclusion of hyperons. In particular, we include $\Lambda$ hyperons in dense matter and neglect contributions from other hyperons, then constrain $E_\mathrm{U}(n_\mathrm{b})$ using nuclear physics and astrophysical observations through a Bayesian inference approach. Our results show that $E_\mathrm{U}(n_\mathrm{b})$ is much smaller than 9$E_\mathrm{sym}(n_\mathrm{b})$, indicating a substantially weaker dependence of the adopted binding energy functional on the U-spin asymmetry than on the corresponding I-spin asymmetry. Consequently, the $\Lambda$ hyperon potential increases significantly with density and becomes repulsive at higher densities, leading to more than 50\% probability for the emergence of $\Lambda$ hyperons in the posterior, which are likely to vanish again at densities $n_\mathrm{b} \gtrsim 5\,n_0$. In scenarios where $\Lambda$ hyperons do emerge, the onset density $n_{\mathrm{b}}^\Lambda$ typically falls in the range $2\,n_0$--$5\,n_0$, corresponding to central densities of neutron stars more massive than $1.0\,\rm{M_\odot}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.01615.title: Testing the wormhole echo hypothesis for GW231123
arxiv.org/abs/2602.01615.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.01615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The short-duration gravitational-wave (GW) event GW231123 has component masses inferred to lie in the pair-instability mass gap and exhibits a burst-like morphology without a clear inspiral phase, making it an interesting target for testing alternatives to the standard binary black hole (BBH) interpretation. Motivated by its phenomenological similarity to GW190521, we test a wormhole-echo interpretation by modeling a leading echo pulse with a phenomenological \texttt{sine-Gaussian} wavepacket. Bayesian model comparison against a BBH interpretation described by the \texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM-SpinTaylor} waveform yields $\ln \mathcal{B}^{\rm Echo}_{\rm BBH}=1.87$. This preference is sensitive to the BBH waveform family and Echo-prior choices, and the observed statistic is not unusual within the targeted BBH-null ensembles. The positive Bayes factor therefore does not provide robust evidence for a wormhole-echo interpretation, with the analyses considered here supporting the standard BBH interpretation of GW231123.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.01933.title: Hadronic description of nuclear matter and neutron star properties
arxiv.org/abs/2603.01933.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.01933v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The composition of the neutron star is one of the most fundamental and long-standing problems in nuclear- and astro-physics. The known properties of nuclear matter, together with the astronomical observations, impose the stringent and interconnected constraints on the theoretical descriptions. In this work, by using the most general quantum hadrodynamics model including $\sigma, \omega, \rho$ and $a_0$ in addition to nucleons, and performing a Bayesian joint analysis of experimental nuclear matter data, the heavy-ion flow pressure, and astrophysical observations including the mass-radius inferences of PSR J0740+6620, PSR J0437$-$4715, PSR J0614$-$3329 and HESS J1731$-$347 and the tidal posterior of GW170817, we point out that the nuclear matter made of only hadrons can provide a unified description of nuclear matter properties and astrophysical observations.In addition, we find that the speed of sound in the GQHD develops a non-monotonic, peak-like structure which is absent in the Walecka-type models TM1, NL3 and FSU-$\delta6.7$. This soft-to-stiff transition, accompanied by a pronounced softening of the symmetry energy, results in small size intermediate mass neutron stars, $R_{1.4}\simeq (11.1-11.4)$~km, together with the maximum mass $(2.2-2.3)M_\odot$, and, to our knowledge, has not been found before in the Walecka-type relativistic mean-field models. What we find here indicate that the sequential measurement of neutron star mass and radius by the next generation facilities, especially that of the intermediate mass neutron stars, is crucial for distinguishing the pure nucleonic stars from the hybrid ones.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.15829.title: Twin-peaked gravitational wave signals from a $\mathcal{Z}_2$ phase transition
arxiv.org/abs/2603.15829.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.15829v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We compute the gravitational wave spectrum from a phase transition associated with the spontaneous breaking of a $\mathcal{Z}_2^{\rm DW}$ symmetry. If the transition is second-order, the only source of gravitational waves is the annihilation of domain walls (biased by quantum gravity) formed after this breaking. However, if the transition is first-order, this yields a twin-peaked signal from both the transition itself and the biased domain wall annihilation. Both scenarios originate when a scalar singlet odd under the $\mathcal{Z}_2^{\rm DW}$ obtains a non-zero vacuum expectation value. An additional $\mathcal{Z}_2^{\rm DM}$ odd scalar doublet strengthens the transition by keeping the singlet scalar in thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model plasma at early times. Additionally, the same scalar doublet produces fermionic dark matter via freeze-in, matching observed dark matter relic density.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.22898.title: Diffuse Supernova Neutrinos with Secret Neutrino Interactions
arxiv.org/abs/2606.22898.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.22898v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB), an isotropic flux arising from the cumulative neutrino emission of all stellar core-collapse events throughout cosmic history, is expected to be detected by next-generation neutrino observatories. As DSNB neutrinos propagate over cosmological distances through the cosmic neutrino background (C$
u$B), they may undergo non-standard neutrino self-interactions ($
u$SI), leaving distinct spectral imprints on the observed flux. In this work, we investigate the impact of scalar ($\phi$)-mediated $
u$SI on the DSNB within a full three-flavor framework that retains the complete PMNS structure. We consider four representative flavor-diagonal coupling structures--universal, $e$-, $\mu$-, and $	au$-specific. The resonant scattering $
u_i
u_k	o\phi	o
u_j
u_l$ off the lightest, relativistic C$
u$B state produces broad spectral depletion whose pattern depends on the coupling structure and the neutrino mass ordering, generating distinctive signatures across the six flavor fluxes. We compute the resulting event spectra at JUNO, Hyper-Kamiokande with gadolinium loading, and DUNE, and derive projected $3\sigma$ sensitivities in the $(m_{\phi},~g)$ parameter plane. We find that these experiments can probe couplings as low as $g\sim10^{-8}$ for $m_\phi\sim100$--$300$ eV, surpassing existing bounds by up to a few orders of magnitude in the sub-100 eV mass range. Moreover, unlike the flavor-blind cosmological and supernova bounds, the DSNB sensitivity is flavor-discriminating, offering a unique opportunity to identify the underlying flavor structure of $

arxiv.org/abs/2607.00137.title: Cosmology with a Non-minimally Coupled Dark Matter Fluid II. Cosmological Perturbations
arxiv.org/abs/2607.00137.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.00137v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We extend our study of a cosmological scenario in which dark matter is non-minimally coupled to gravity at the fluid level. In previous work, we showed that this interaction can drive an early phase of accelerated expansion, addressing the horizon and flatness problems, and can also lead to a cosmological bounce in the presence of negative spatial curvature. Here we analyse the evolution of linear perturbations in this framework. We derive the equations governing scalar, vector and tensor perturbations, and obtain analytic solutions in the relevant cosmological regimes. We find that perturbations generated during the accelerated expansion phase produce a strongly blue scalar power spectrum and are therefore incompatible with observations. By contrast, if primordial fluctuations are generated during the contracting phase of a bouncing solution, the model yields an approximately scale-invariant scalar power spectrum while keeping the tensor-to-scalar ratio compatible with current bounds. Although our treatment relies on simplifying approximations that should be refined in future work, these results indicate that an observationally viable primordial spectrum can be obtained only with a bouncing solution, and hence with a non-singular early-time evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.25932.title: Analytic backreaction of a scalar wig on a Schwarzschild black hole
arxiv.org/abs/2607.25932.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.25932v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We analytically determine the leading backreaction of a spherically symmetric massive complex scalar quasi-bound state (with mass $\mu$) on a Schwarzschild black hole with (initial) gravitational radius $r_0$. Working in the small-coupling regime, $r_0 \mu \ll 1$, we evaluate the stress-energy tensor of the fundamental scalar $s$-wave and solve the Einstein equations through quadratic order in its amplitude in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates. We also determine the small-mass quasi-resonant frequency of the fundamental $s$-wave analytically by matched asymptotic expansions and validate it numerically using Leaver's method. Unlike steady-state treatments, the calculation retains the exponential decay of the quasi-bound state. We obtain explicit expressions for the metric perturbations and Misner-Sharp mass and derive the evolution of the future outer trapping horizon. The black-hole mass grows monotonically with the decaying horizon flux and saturates when the finite scalar cloud has been absorbed, with the decrease of the cloud mass exactly balancing the horizon growth at the perturbative order considered. We also determine the domain in which the scalar small-coupling approximation and the gravitational perturbative expansion are simultaneously valid.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.17395.title: Seeding baryonic dark matter
arxiv.org/abs/2608.17395.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.17395v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: It has been proposed that primordial quark pellets or PQPs --ultra-dense quark-matter mini- stars-- formed at $T\sim 1$ GeV may be a good candidate accounting for the dark matter of the universe. If correct, dark matter would consist of very compact objects with a maximum mass of $10^{-2} \ M_\odot$ and radii of approximately 100 m, although smaller objects would be much more abundant and encompass the bulk of the dark matter content. Here we describe a viable formation mechanism based on the enhancement of the local baryon density when supra-horizon Peccei-Quinn domain walls formed at an earlier epoch sweep and accumulate quarks and gluons before entering the horizon. Assuming an efficient baryon concentration by contracting Peccei-Quinn domain walls, we derive the resulting primordial quark pellet mass spectrum, minimum mass and cosmological abundance.

phys.org/news/2026-10-ai.html.title: Want to use AI to improve your work? Have it disagree with you
phys.org/news/2026-10-ai.html.excerpt: Knowledge workers such as scientists, teachers, lawyers and business leaders are increasingly using generative artificial intelligence applications for tasks that demand imagination, creativity and problem-solving. Ironically, perhaps, recent research shows that people who interact with generative AI for work tasks can end up not thinking critically. They can surrender to AI's quick and confident answers, which can lead to speedy but low-quality solutions.

phys.org/news/2026-10-ancient-sea-reveal.title: Ancient sea levels reveal when the Earth's poles went wandering
phys.org/news/2026-10-ancient-sea-reveal.excerpt: Earth's poles do not always stay in the same place. For example, a region once near the North Pole can end up near the equator, and an area near the equator can shift up toward the pole. This is known as true polar wander (TPW), and it's when Earth's crust and mantle shift together relative to its spin axis.

phys.org/news/2026-10-fluorescent-screen.title: Fluorescent test speeds screening of thousands of enzyme variants that modify plant compounds
phys.org/news/2026-10-fluorescent-screen.excerpt: Many natural plant compounds have promising health-related properties, but their poor water solubility can limit how effectively they are absorbed and used. In previous work, researchers discovered an enzyme from Bacillus subtilis, called phenolic phosphate synthetase (BsPPS), that can attach phosphate groups to a broad range of phenolic compounds. This modification can help make these compounds more water-soluble and support the development of improved nutraceuticals and related products.

phys.org/news/2026-10-millions-years-evo.title: Millions of years of evolution guide AI search for pollution-fighting enzymes
phys.org/news/2026-10-millions-years-evo.excerpt: Databases around the world contain information on millions upon millions of enzymes that have the potential to degrade pollutants like plastic. Scientists at Murdoch University's Bioplastics Innovation Hub are combining machine learning technology and biochemistry to identify which of these enzymes have the potential to break down plastic and other harmful pollutants.

phys.org/news/2026-10-mangrove-big-busin.title: Mangrove restoration is becoming big business, but benefits don't always reach local people
phys.org/news/2026-10-mangrove-big-busin.excerpt: On Pakistan's Indus delta coast, a 350,000-hectare (865,000-acre) mangrove project is turning a growing forest into something that can be sold to companies thousands of miles away: carbon credits.

phys.org/news/2026-10-white-nationalism-.title: White nationalism's appeal runs deeper than partisan politics
phys.org/news/2026-10-white-nationalism-.excerpt: As Americans prepared to celebrate the nation's 250th birthday on the morning of July 4, sobering images flashed across their phones and TV screens. Hundreds of masked men marched through the streets of Washington carrying flags and chanting "Reclaim America!" It soon became clear from the logos on their identical baseball caps that the marchers were members of Patriot Front, a white nationalist group.

phys.org/news/2026-10-enzymes-sturdy-bea.title: Enzymes become sturdy beads that could support more sustainable chemical production
phys.org/news/2026-10-enzymes-sturdy-bea.excerpt: Thanks to enzyme-based biocatalysis, an enormous range of pharmaceutical active ingredients and other complex molecules can be synthesized in an environmentally friendly manner. Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) have now developed a technology that allows to assemble enzymes into millimeter-sized, storable beads. In this process, the enzymes not only act as catalysts but also constitute the beads' material itself. In a further variant, the enzyme networks can be combined with living cells. A patent application has been filed for the technology. The results have been published in Advanced Materials.

phys.org/news/2026-10-stars-infrared-exp.title: How stars shine: Infrared observations expose gaps in models of how stars distribute their light
phys.org/news/2026-10-stars-infrared-exp.excerpt: Astronomers using Georgia State University's Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array have found that nearby stars darken toward their edges more strongly at near-infrared wavelengths than predicted by several widely used models of stellar atmospheres, providing a new benchmark for understanding how stars are structured.

phys.org/news/2026-10-qa-red-squirrels-e.title: Q&A: Why are red squirrels endangered—and can we save them?
phys.org/news/2026-10-qa-red-squirrels-e.excerpt: The red squirrel was once a familiar sight across Britain. Today, it has disappeared from much of its former range. Dr. Kat Hamill, senior lecturer in zoology at Nottingham Trent University, explains what has happened to one of Britain's most recognizable native mammals—and whether science and conservation can help bring it back.

phys.org/news/2026-10-space-circadian-rh.title: What space travel teaches us about sleep and circadian rhythms
phys.org/news/2026-10-space-circadian-rh.excerpt: On Earth, most of us rarely have to think about the signals that keep our internal clocks aligned. The sun rises, daylight changes, darkness arrives and morning comes again.

phys.org/news/2026-10-iron-age-skulls-re.title: Iron Age skulls reveal some babies had flat head syndrome—long before the 'Back to Sleep' campaign
phys.org/news/2026-10-iron-age-skulls-re.excerpt: Nearly 3,000 years ago, in central Italy, dozens of Picene people were laid to rest curled up on their sides, as if asleep. When their eternal slumber was disturbed thousands of years later, researchers noted a curiously familiar pattern, one many modern parents and doctors fret over: As infants, many of them had developed a flat spot on their heads.

phys.org/news/2026-10-moon.html.title: New research shows how water would behave on the moon
phys.org/news/2026-10-moon.html.excerpt: As humanity looks toward future bases on the moon, plant cultivation will be critical for sustaining life there. Plants can provide food, oxygen, medicine, water purification and waste recycling, making them indispensable for lunar development.

phys.org/news/2026-10-multilingual-reade.title: Multilingual readers report higher enjoyment and more daily reading, survey finds
phys.org/news/2026-10-multilingual-reade.excerpt: The U.K.'s National Year of Reading is asking people across the country to "go all in" on reading. But this invitation raises questions for many families: reading what, in which language and in what form?

phys.org/news/2026-10-world-oceans-metho.title: How much are the world's oceans warming? New method reveals double-digit percentage gaps from climate models
phys.org/news/2026-10-world-oceans-metho.excerpt: The world's oceans behave like a thermometer: As the water warms, it expands and sea levels rise. Geodesy researchers at the University of Bonn are able to measure this and determine how much the oceans are warming. For individual ocean basins, their method has revealed significant deviations from model calculations—in some cases in the double-digit percentage range.

phys.org/news/2026-10-reveals-national-c.title: New study reveals how national cyber positions can shape the future of international law
phys.org/news/2026-10-reveals-national-c.excerpt: Nations should do more to reduce uncertainty about the legal value of their positions on cyber activities, a new study says.

phys.org/news/2026-10-reality-lab-grown-.title: A 'reality check' for lab-grown human embryo models
phys.org/news/2026-10-reality-lab-grown-.excerpt: University of Sydney researchers have developed a new way to test how closely lab-grown biological models resemble real human embryos, finding that while some models perform well, none yet fully capture the complexity of early human development.

phys.org/news/2026-10-multitasking-magen.title: Multitasking in magenta: Colored solar panels could help farms grow crops and generate electricity on shared land
phys.org/news/2026-10-multitasking-magen.excerpt: Broccoli grown under magenta solar panels absorbed sunlight more efficiently than plants grown out in the open, according to a study to be published Oct. 2 in Cell Reports Physical Science.

phys.org/news/2026-10-tomato-wilt-virus-.title: First U.S. tomato spotted wilt virus clone could speed development of disease-resistant crops
phys.org/news/2026-10-tomato-wilt-virus-.excerpt: New technology from Texas A&M AgriLife Research could be a major step toward bringing disease-resistant peppers and tomatoes to growers' fields and lowering costs at grocery stores.

phys.org/news/2026-10-natural-material-b.title: Natural-material bricks aim to give urban birds alternatives to nesting with trash
phys.org/news/2026-10-natural-material-b.excerpt: It's spring, and Australian birds are building their nests. But with what? Alongside grass and twigs, birds are collecting our trash. In 2023, a global study found litter in the nests of 176 different bird species, with common culprits including cigarette butts, plastic bags and fishing nets.

phys.org/news/2026-10-uranium-rare-tripl.title: Uranium forms rare triple bond with carbon in newly isolated compound
phys.org/news/2026-10-uranium-rare-tripl.excerpt: In a study published in Nature Chemistry, an international team of researchers from Germany and the U.K., including chemists from The University of Manchester, has synthesized and characterized what they describe as the first isolable uranium Fischer-type carbyne, a compound in which carbon forms an unusual triple-bond interaction with uranium.

phys.org/news/2026-10-survey-burnout-ind.title: Survey finds burnout is top challenge for independent local news publishers
phys.org/news/2026-10-survey-burnout-ind.excerpt: More than 55% of publishers of independent local news organizations cite burnout as a concern, and about 52% view balancing journalism with business operations as one of their most pressing challenges, a new survey finds.

phys.org/news/2026-10-protons-energy-pul.title: Protons ride moving waves to reach record energy with long-pulse lasers
phys.org/news/2026-10-protons-energy-pul.excerpt: Imagine a proton catching a wave and surfing it to gain speed. While the imagery may seem wild, the premise of laser-driven ion acceleration has promise as an alternative to conventional accelerators. However, the ultrathin targets used to drive this increase in ion energy are vulnerable to the weak prepulse that precedes the main high-intensity laser pulse, meaning an adaptation in the process is necessary.

phys.org/news/2026-10-australia-native-b.title: Are Australia's native bees thriving or declining?

livescience.com/planet-earth/evolution/a.title: Animals may have evolved 200 million years earlier than previously thought, new study suggests
livescience.com/planet-earth/evolution/a.excerpt: After using a technique called molecular clock analysis, researchers have proposed that the origin of animals could be 200 million years earlier than thought.

livescience.com/planet-earth/how-prepare.title: How prepared are you for a disaster?
livescience.com/planet-earth/how-prepare.excerpt: From emergency kits to evacuation plans, Live Science asks readers how prepared they are for the unexpected.

sciencealert.com/finally-rose-tinted-sol.title: Finally: Rose-Tinted Solar Panels Could Let Crops And Electricity Share The Same Land
sciencealert.com/finally-rose-tinted-sol.excerpt: (Silvia Ma Lu) Could this be the future of solar farming? ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.

physicsworld.com/a/quiz-of-the-week-how-.title: Quiz of the week: how are researchers making weather predictions more accurate?
physicsworld.com/a/quiz-of-the-week-how-.excerpt: Have you been keeping up to date with physics news? Try our short quiz to find out The post Quiz of the week: how are researchers making weather predictions more accurate? appeared first on Physics World .

physicsworld.com/a/abdus-salam-pakistans.title: Abdus Salam: Pakistan’s first (and so far only) Nobel prize-winner
physicsworld.com/a/abdus-salam-pakistans.excerpt: Matin Durrani looks at the work of Abdus Salam, who was born a century ago this year. The post Abdus Salam: Pakistan’s first (and so far only) Nobel prize-winner appeared first on Physics World .

statnews.com/2026/10/02/nobel-prize-2026.title: What it’s like to wait for the call from the Nobel Prize committee
statnews.com/2026/10/02/nobel-prize-2026.excerpt: Ahead of this year's Nobel Prize announcements, STAT chatted with Mary-Claire King, who discovered the BRCA cancer mutations and is frequently mentioned in prize predictions.

statnews.com/2026/10/02/youth-opioid-tre.title: Access to addiction meds for young people has improved — but retention hasn’t
statnews.com/2026/10/02/youth-opioid-tre.excerpt: Only a small fraction of young people with opioid use disorder receive addiction medications, and few stay on them for long, a study finds.

statnews.com/2026/10/02/ebola-outbreak-c.title: An Ebola treatment center was burned down as the death toll in Congo passes 4,000
statnews.com/2026/10/02/ebola-outbreak-c.excerpt: Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 4,000 people, authorities said, as they struggle to contain what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

statnews.com/2026/10/02/biotech-news-lil.title: STAT+: Lilly bypasses Australian pharmacies with DTC model
statnews.com/2026/10/02/biotech-news-lil.excerpt: Eli Lilly is launching LillyDirect to deliver Mounjaro straight to Australian patients’ doors — and local doctors and pharmacists aren’t thrilled.

astronomy.com/observing/best-lighting-to.title: How can I reduce my personal contribution to light pollution?
astronomy.com/observing/best-lighting-to.excerpt: What type of lighting emits the least amount of light pollution? Peter BladoTacoma, Washington First, use a good lighting fixture, one that is a “full cutoff.” That means there is no direct upgoing light at all. It generally also means there is very little light just below the horizontal, which is the kind of light Continue reading "How can I reduce my personal contribution to light pollution?" The post How can I reduce my personal contribution to light pollution? appeared first on Astronomy Magazine .

earthsky.org/space/alien-radio-signal-k2.title: Is this an alien radio signal from a super-Earth exoplanet?
earthsky.org/space/alien-radio-signal-k2.excerpt: Did China's FAST radio telescope detect an alien radio signal coming from the super-Earth exoplanet K2-155 d? Probably not. The post Is this an alien radio signal from a super-Earth exoplanet? first appeared on EarthSky .

earthsky.org/space/earthlike-planet-with.title: Could an Earthlike planet with 2 stars be nearby?
earthsky.org/space/earthlike-planet-with.excerpt: A new astronomical model has found that an Earthlike planet could have a stable and potentially habitable orbit around a star in a nearby 2-star system. The post Could an Earthlike planet with 2 stars be nearby? first appeared on EarthSky .

earthsky.org/human-world/october-birthst.title: October birthstone: Colorful opal and tourmaline
earthsky.org/human-world/october-birthst.excerpt: Take your pick: the October birthstone is either the striking iridescent opal or the many-colored tourmaline. Learn the lore of these pretty gemstones here. The post October birthstone: Colorful opal and tourmaline first appeared on EarthSky .

9.headline: Australia Deploys Dynamic Ice Sheet Model for Climate Simulations
9.summary: ACCESS‑NRI released a full ISSM workflow on NCI’s Gadi supercomputer, enabling Australian researchers to model two‑way ice‑ocean‑atmosphere interactions for future climate projections.
highlights: ACCESS‑NRI unveiled four new components of the Ice Sheet and Sea‑level System Model (ISSM) workflow for Australian users
The pyISSM Python API lets scientists configure and run ISSM models entirely in Python on NCI Gadi
The Cryosphere Community Data Pool (CCD) provides open‑access cryospheric datasets for the national community

hi_orion_nebula.headline: HI Mapping Reveals Expanding Shell in the Extended Orion Nebula
hi_orion_nebula.summary: High‑resolution 21‑centimeter observations resolve neutral atomic hydrogen in the Orion Nebula, uncovering a shell with only ~100 solar masses of gas.
highlights: Neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) imaged at one‑arcminute resolution (~0.12 pc)
Shell mass estimated at 100 solar masses, ten‑times lower than [CII]‑based estimates
Discovery of a secondary bubble and a four‑parsec linear protrusion

2609_01784v1.headline: Isolated Binary Evolution Naturally Shapes Low‑Mass Black‑Hole Merger Mass Ratios
2609_01784v1.summary: Binary‑population models using POSYDON predict a broad asymmetric peak at q≈0.5‑0.7 and a near‑equal‑mass component, matching the observed low‑mass binary‑black‑hole subpopulation.
highlights: Models favor asymmetric mass ratios with a peak near q≈0.5‑0.7
A secondary near‑equal‑mass peak arises from double‑core common‑envelope and contact channels
Predicted q distribution aligns with gravitational‑wave observations of low‑mass binaries

nsc_bulge_fossil.headline: Milky Way Nuclear Star Cluster May Not Be a Simple Bulge Fossil Fragment
nsc_bulge_fossil.summary: New analysis shows the Milky Way nuclear star cluster shares chemical ties with the inner bulge but differs from proposed bulge fossil fragments like Terzan 5 and Liller 1.
highlights: Broad metallicity spread in the NSC mirrors the bulge field but alone cannot confirm a fossil‑fragment origin
Metal‑rich, alpha‑enhanced stars in the NSC contrast with near‑solar alpha abundances of Terzan 5 and Liller 1
Chemo‑dynamical and spatial segregation tests suggest the NSC formed through mixed in‑situ star formation, migration, and

tev_delayed_flare_1es1959_650.headline: LHAASO-WCDA Detects Five-Day TeV Lag in Blazar 1ES 1959+650
tev_delayed_flare_1es1959_650.summary: A day‑scale hard lag of about five days between GeV and TeV γ‑rays was observed from the HBL 1ES 1959+650 during early 2024.
highlights: LHAASO‑WCDA real‑time monitoring triggered three TeV flares in 2024, including the first on 2024 February 9.
Cross‑correlation analysis shows a >3σ correlation with a delay Δt = 5.0 ± 2.1 days, TeV emission lagging GeV.
The delayed flare exhibited the softest TeV spectrum (intrinsic index Γ = 3.16 ± 0.18) compared with the earlier hard flare

gasflows_sfms_mzr_link.headline: Neutral Gas Flows Linked to Star‑Forming Main Sequence and Metallicity Offsets in 6,000 DESI Galaxies
gasflows_sfms_mzr_link.summary: A study of ~6,000 star‑forming galaxies using Na I D absorption finds that neutral‑gas inflows and outflows produce distinct sSFR and metallicity shifts relative to the SFMS and MZR.
highlights: Outflow hosts (v₍flow₎ ≤ ‑50 km s⁻¹) boost specific star‑formation rates by 0.25‑0.40 dex and raise central metallicities by
Slow inflow hosts (0 < v₍flow₎ < 100 km s⁻¹) increase sSFRs by 0.20‑0.30 dex without notable metallicity changes.
Fast inflow hosts (v₍flow₎ ≥ 100 km s⁻¹) show weaker SFR enhancement and modest metallicity dilution.
Gas‑flow galaxies exhibit systematic offsets in the 4000 Å break strength (Dₙ4000) compared with matched controls.

ru_isotope_late_veneer.institution: Institute(s) of the authors of arXiv:2609.02269v1
ru_isotope_late_veneer.headline: Ruthenium Isotope Split Reveals Mostly Non‑Carbonaceous Late Veneer on Earth
ru_isotope_late_veneer.summary: High‑precision Ru isotope measurements show non‑carbonaceous meteorites follow an s‑process line, while carbonaceous irons form a distinct cluster, suggesting a predominantly NC late‑veneer source for Earth.
highlights: NC meteorites align on an s‑process mixing line in three‑isotope diagrams
CC irons cluster off the NC line, indicating an r‑process excess
Bulk silicate Earth plots on the NC line, implying NC‑dominated late veneer

7.headline: Disorder Can Boost Stability in Power Grids, Brain Networks and Ecosystems
7.summary: Northwestern physicists show that moderate heterogeneity in complex networks often enhances resilience, overturning the long‑held belief that uniformity is optimal.
highlights: A new mathematical framework identifies when node or link variation stabilizes networks
Random differences sometimes outperform perfectly uniform configurations
The effect spans power grids, neuronal circuits, flocking models, architected materials and ecological webs

nanobone_bone_regeneration.headline: Biodegradable Nanobone Boosts Bone Regrowth by Up to 80% in Preclinical Tests
nanobone_bone_regeneration.summary: A calcium‑aluminosilicate nanomaterial developed by University of Sydney researchers accelerates bone formation, activating latent TGF‑β1 and clotting within seconds.
highlights: Nanobone generated ~80% more new bone than control after eight weeks
Activates dormant Transforming Growth Factor β1 at ~10‑fold higher levels
Triggers rapid blood clotting in ~30 seconds, stabilizing injury sites

2609_01796v1.headline: Massive Mergers Trigger Long‑Lived Tumbling of Dark Matter Halos
2609_01796v1.summary: Simulations and TNG50 data show that major galaxy mergers can induce rapid and persistent figure rotation in dark matter halos, preserving a memory of the last merger.
highlights: Transient rotation peaks at 10°‑60° Gyr⁻¹ during satellite infall
Steady tumbling persists at 2°‑40° Gyr⁻¹ for 6‑8 Gyr post‑merger
Radial mergers without orbital angular momentum still drive figure rotation
All six TNG50 halos altered quadrupole orientation during major mergers

turbulent_reconnection_solar_flares.headline: Turbulent Reconnection Accelerates Solar Flare Electrons to ~90 keV
turbulent_reconnection_solar_flares.summary: High‑resolution MHD simulations show that turbulence‑driven compression structures rapidly boost thermal electrons in solar flares to energies near 90 keV, producing observed power‑law spectra.
highlights: Thermal electrons at the flare current sheet and loop top reach ~90 keV
Energy spectra display power‑law indices matching typical flare observations
Acceleration is driven by turbulent compression structures, not termination shocks

ancient_microbe_asgard_imaging.headline: Ancient Stromatolite Microbe Partnership Offers Clues to Origin of Complex Life
ancient_microbe_asgard_imaging.summary: Researchers imaged an Asgard archaeon linked to a bacterium inside modern stromatolites, revealing a possible model for early eukaryotic evolution.
highlights: First direct images of an Asgard archaeon physically connected to a bacterium via nanotubes
Microbe named Nerearchaeum marumarumayae isolated from Shark Bay’s living stromatolites
Electron cryotomography and deep‑learning analysis revealed nutrient‑exchange structures
Study published in Current Biology (2026) after five‑year cultivation effort

new_hall_effect_form.headline: In‑Plane Anomalous Hall Effect Defies Century‑Old Assumption
new_hall_effect_form.summary: Carnegie Mellon physicists have demonstrated an in‑plane anomalous Hall effect, proving the Hall response can arise without a perpendicular magnetic field.
highlights: The team used atomically thin TaIrTe4 coupled with magnetic Cr2Ge2Te6 to generate the new Hall signal.
Both conventional and unconventional Hall voltages were detected in a single ultrathin device.
The discovery could enable planar magnetic sensors that measure multiple field directions simultaneously.

plasmonic_time_crystal.headline: All‑Optical Photonic Time Crystal Demonstrated Using Plasmonic Metamaterial
plasmonic_time_crystal.summary: Researchers in France and Germany have built the first all‑optical photonic time crystal, modulating light at terahertz frequencies within picoseconds.
highlights: The nanostructure uses gold‑capped cavities on an indium‑antimony semiconductor to trap surface plasmons.
THz pulses from the TELBE source at the ELBE accelerator achieved picosecond‑scale optical modulation.
The device halves photon dissipation, opening pathways to THz amplifiers and novel lasers.

bat_dual_antibody_genes.headline: Bats Possess Duplicate Antibody Genes, Explaining Viral Tolerance
bat_dual_antibody_genes.summary: Researchers found that over 500 vesper bat species carry two distinct immunoglobulin heavy‑chain gene sets, a mammalian immune feature never seen before.
highlights: More than 500 vesper bat species have duplicated heavy‑chain antibody loci.
This dual gene system is absent in all other studied mammals.
Study published in Science Advances (2026) by Tulane, Stanford and CDC collaborators.
The discovery suggests a novel mechanism for bats to tolerate many viruses.

immune_switch_aging.headline: Blocking EP2 Receptor in Macrophages Reverses Age‑Related Decline in Mice
immune_switch_aging.summary: Scientists found that disabling the EP2 receptor on tissue‑resident macrophages restores neutrophil clearance, reducing inflammation and keeping multiple organs youthful in aged mice.
highlights: EP2 deletion restored macrophage ability to engulf senescent neutrophils
Older mice lacking EP2 stayed leaner, stronger, and performed memory tests like young mice
Blood‑protein profiles of EP2‑deficient old mice resembled those of youthful controls

electron_spin_surface_reactions.headline: Electron Spin Enables Magnetic Control of Hydrogen Surface Reactions
electron_spin_surface_reactions.summary: Researchers showed that aligning hydrogen electron spin with a magnetic nickel surface can boost adsorption rates by over sevenfold, offering a new reaction control lever.
highlights: Spin‑polarized hydrogen beam was directed at a ferromagnetic nickel surface
Parallel spin orientation increased hydrogen adsorption more than seven times versus perpendicular
Effect vanished on non‑magnetic copper, confirming magnetic origin
Spin alignment also accelerated hydrogen‑deuterium abstraction reactions
External magnetic fields provide a tunable lever for surface chemistry

quantum_material_beating_signal.headline: Korean Team Uncovers Origin of Beating Signal in Topological Insulator Nanowires
quantum_material_beating_signal.summary: Researchers identified that overlapping oscillations from topological surface states and a 2D electron gas cause the puzzling beating observed in Sb‑doped Bi₂Se₃ nanowires.
highlights: Beating arises from superposition of Aharonov‑Bohm oscillations of topological surface states and a 2DEG layer.
Machine‑learning analysis separated the two frequency components, confirming distinct paths with different cross‑sectional areas.
The result provides a definitive criterion for interpreting quantum transport signals in topological insulator devices.

saturn_decagon_discovery_2026_09_03.headline: NASA Finds Giant Decagon Wave Encircling Saturn’s South Pole
saturn_decagon_discovery_2026_09_03.summary: Hubble observations reveal a growing ten‑sided atmospheric wave around Saturn’s south pole, a counterpart to the long‑known northern hexagon, first seen in 2023.
highlights: The decagon was first hinted at in 2023 Hubble images and became clearer by 2025.
It lies within a powerful jet stream and extends through multiple atmospheric layers.
The discovery was enabled by NASA’s OPAL program’s annual Hubble imaging of the outer planets.

ai_suggests_new_physics_experiments.headline: AI designs physics experiments that outperform human‑crafted setups
ai_suggests_new_physics_experiments.summary: A new AI system can automatically combine laboratory components to propose experiments that deliver more precise results than traditional human‑designed designs.
highlights: AI algorithm generated a viable quantum‑optics setup that humans missed
The method improved electron‑microscopy designs, offering clearer images
AI‑driven proposals have already enhanced fusion reactor concepts and gravitational‑wave detector sensitivity

dual_qubit_design.headline: MIT engineers dual‑purpose “arm qubit” to boost speed and slash quantum errors
dual_qubit_design.summary: Researchers at Massachusetts Institute of Technology have simulated a superconducting qubit that separates data storage and interaction, promising faster, higher‑fidelity operations.
highlights: Dual‑purpose design splits data mode and arm mode for dedicated storage and coupling
Quarton coupler provides strong nonlinear coupling while suppressing unwanted mixing
Simulations show state‑of‑the‑art coherence times and accelerated gate speeds

bacterial_nanoplatform_cancer_prevention.headline: Engineered Bacterial Nanoplatform Reprograms Spleen Cells to Halt Cancer Recurrence
bacterial_nanoplatform_cancer_prevention.summary: A bio‑engineered Mycobacterium coated with human serum albumin redirects splenic myelopoiesis, inducing trained immunity that prevents post‑surgical tumor relapse in mice.
highlights: t‑SMC nanoplatform targets spleen via intravenous delivery and releases a TLR7/8 agonist.
Reprogrammed splenic macrophages and stem cells acquire antitumor phenotype and migrate to tumor sites.
In a colon‑cancer recurrence model, 50% of mice showed no tumor return and 62.5% survived long‑term.
Approach converts “cold” tumors into “hot” ones, enhancing response to anti‑PD‑L1 checkpoint blockade.

saturn_decagon_confirmation.headline: Saturn’s South Pole Decagon Confirmed by Hubble Observations
saturn_decagon_confirmation.summary: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured a fully defined 10‑sided atmospheric wave over Saturn’s south pole, confirming a new planetary phenomenon.
highlights: Decagon first hinted in 2023 Hubble data and sharpened in 2025 images
Amateur and professional astronomers identified the feature in 2024 ground‑based photos
The wave spans multiple atmospheric layers within a powerful jet stream
Study published in Science Advances, September 2026

2609_03051v1.headline: Collective Collapse Can Yield Multiple Primordial Black Holes, Simulations Show
2609_03051v1.summary: New 3+1 numerical-relativity simulations reveal that neighboring curvature perturbations may merge or split, producing single or double primordial black holes.
highlights: Neighbouring curvature peaks can collapse into a single PBH or form a pair of PBHs
A nonspherical quasi‑local compaction diagnostic based on Hawking mass predicts collapse outcomes
The empirical threshold for PBH formation is near \(\mathcal K_{\rm form,c}\approx0.56\)
Maximum curvature alone does not dictate whether one or multiple PBHs form

lvk_o4_catalogue.headline: Fourth LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Run Yields ~100 New Gravitational‑Wave Detections
lvk_o4_catalogue.summary: The O4 observing run added roughly one hundred fresh mergers, including the loudest signals yet and novel source types, expanding astrophysical insight.
highlights: ~100 new binary‑black‑hole and neutron‑star mergers catalogued
Loudest gravitational‑wave signals recorded to date
Evidence for multiple subpopulations of merging compact binaries

2609_03011v1.headline: Realistic AGN Disk Simulations Reveal How Star Collisions Drive QPEs
2609_03011v1.summary: Two‑dimensional radiation‑hydrodynamic models show that bow‑shock breakout in puffed‑up AGN disks produces X‑ray flares lasting ~10 % of the orbital period, matching QPE observations.
highlights: Simulations use realistic sub‑Eddington AGN disk structure with atmosphere extending to z/r≈1.
Shock breakout at z/r≈0.7 yields flare durations ≈10 % of the star’s orbital period.
More oblique star‑disk impacts generate longer, brighter X‑ray eruptions.
Disk surface density Σ∝r² leads to collisional energy scaling E∝P^{2/3}, reproducing the luminosity‑period trend.

2609_03007v1.headline: Tidal Forces Trigger Chaos in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals Around Supermassive Black Holes
2609_03007v1.summary: A new arXiv preprint shows that external tidal fields break Kerr symmetry, causing chaotic resonances in EMRIs that could affect future gravitational‑wave observations.
highlights: Tidally deformed EMRIs exhibit non‑integrable geodesic dynamics
Poincaré maps reveal two plateaus whose widths grow with tidal field amplitude
Orbit orientation relative to the tidal field strongly influences chaotic behavior

2609_03062v1.headline: DESI DR2 Data Revives Interest in Dynamical Dark Energy Over Dark‑Sector Interactions
2609_03062v1.summary: New DESI DR2, CMB, and supernova measurements favor evolving dark‑energy models while diminishing evidence for a coupling between dark matter and dark energy.
highlights: Interacting $w_0w_a$CDM model with $Q=\beta H\rho_{\rm de}$ shows no significant fit improvement over dynamical dark energy alone.
Thawing and generalized emergent dark‑energy (GEDE) trajectories prefer sizable couplings of opposite signs, unlike the mirage
DESI DR2 combined with Planck and ACT data strengthens the case for a time‑varying dark‑energy equation of state.
Predicted growth signatures differ markedly: enhanced matter clustering for interacting thawing, strong suppression for

2609_03089v1.headline: JWST NIRSpec IFU Maps Reveal Stellar Motions in Three Time‑Delay Lenses
2609_03089v1.summary: Spatially resolved kinematics from JWST‑NIRSpec IFU for HE0435‑1223, PG1115+080 and WFI2033‑4723 tighten mass models, cutting velocity‑dispersion uncertainty to 2.4 %.
highlights: Kinematic maps achieve 6‑11 % total uncertainties per spatial bin
PG1115+080 classified as a fast rotator, the other two as slow rotators
Aperture‑integrated velocity dispersions agree within 0.9σ of previous TDCOSMO values
Data will feed the upcoming TDCOSMO 2026 milestone cosmology analysis

2609_03144v1.headline: Thick CO2‑ or SO2‑Rich Atmosphere Could Survive on Lava World TOI‑561 b
2609_03144v1.summary: New PROTEUS simulations suggest the ultra‑short‑period planet TOI‑561 b may retain a dense CO₂‑ or SO₂‑dominated atmosphere over gigayears despite extreme stellar heating.
highlights: JWST data favor a thick volatile envelope above a global magma ocean
Successful models require a small iron core (≤ 0.40 core radius fraction) and low hydrodynamic escape efficiency (ε ≲ 10⁻³)
Atmospheric pressure today could reach 10³‑10⁴ bar with mean molecular weight of 38‑60 g mol⁻¹

quantum_gravity_experiment.headline: Quantum Galileo Interferometer Confirms Equivalence Principle for 20,000‑Atom Bose‑Einstein Condensate
quantum_gravity_experiment.summary: Physicists at Ben‑Gurion University used a novel interferometer to show that a chilled rubidium cloud obeys Einstein’s equivalence principle in free fall.
highlights: Quantum Galileo Interferometer (QGI) splits a Bose‑Einstein condensate into free‑fall and levitated paths
Interference phase shift matches predictions of the equivalence principle
Experiment employed ~20,000 rubidium atoms cooled near absolute zero

jwst_miri_atmosphere_toi_431b.headline: JWST MIRI Detects Possible Atmosphere on Ultra‑Hot Lava Planet TOI‑431b
jwst_miri_atmosphere_toi_431b.summary: A single JWST MIRI/LRS secondary‑eclipse observation measured an 81 ± 16 ppm depth, suggesting TOI‑431b may retain a thin atmosphere despite its scorching surface.
highlights: Eclipse depth of 81 ± 16 ppm translates to a brightness temperature of 1967⁺²³⁷₋₂⁵³ K
The brightness‑temperature ratio is 0.81 ± 0.10, lower than a bare‑rock model predicts
Comparison with Spitzer data shows a 1.2 σ higher ratio, supporting atmospheric heat redistribution

targeted_search_frbs_magnetars_elliptica.headline: Targeted GBT Survey Finds No Magnetar FRBs in Nearby Elliptical Galaxies
targeted_search_frbs_magnetars_elliptica.summary: A high‑sensitivity L‑band search of five massive ellipticals using GREENBURST and the VEGAS backend detected a background FRB but no magnetar bursts, tightening rate limits.
highlights: FRB 20240817A detected toward M49 (NGC 4472) with 15 ms width and DM = 983 cm⁻³ pc
A cluster of three low‑significance pulses near M49 shows plausible DM = 150‑160 cm⁻³ pc
Joint upper limit on intrinsic burst rate in globular clusters set at R₀ < 0.028 hr⁻¹

bacterial_outer_membrane_proteins.headline: Cryo‑EM snapshots show SurA reshaping to deliver outer‑membrane proteins to the BAM complex
bacterial_outer_membrane_proteins.summary: Researchers used cryo‑electron microscopy to capture four structural states of the SurA‑BAM complex, revealing how SurA’s domains reposition to hand off unfolded proteins for membrane insertion.
highlights: Four distinct cryo‑EM structures of SurA bound to BAM were resolved, showing Core‑only, P1‑visible, P2‑visible, and combined
The flexible P1 domain regulates the Core’s cargo‑binding activity while P2 contacts BamE to bring SurA closer to the assembly
Mutations that disrupt the SurA‑BamE interaction markedly reduce outer‑membrane protein assembly, highlighting a potential

brain_development_2026_09_04.headline: UCLA researchers uncover how metabolism and thalamic signals steer radial glia to shape the human cortex
brain_development_2026_09_04.summary: UCLA scientists show that early brain stem cells integrate glucose‑driven metabolic cues and direct thalamic contacts to decide which cortical neurons to produce.
highlights: Radial glia rely on the pentose phosphate pathway, linking glucose metabolism to cell‑type decisions
Early thalamic projections physically touch radial glia, boosting excitatory upper‑layer neuron formation
NRXN1 mutations alter thalamic signaling, offering a model for autism‑related cortical development

2609_03012v1.headline: Universal CMB Phase Coherence Persists Across All Inflation Energy Scales
2609_03012v1.summary: New analysis shows that the cosmic microwave background’s acoustic peak structure retains identical phase coherence regardless of the inflationary energy scale.
highlights: Phase coherence of primordial perturbations is fixed by the observed primordial spectrum
Curvature perturbation remains conserved on super‑Hubble scales
Result holds for any single‑field inflation scenario and subsequent expansion history

comet_birth_observed.headline: Centaur 450P/LONEOS Shows First Comet‑Like Activity Near Sun
comet_birth_observed.summary: Astronomers observed the centaur 450P/LONEOS developing a bright coma as it approached perihelion, linking inactive centaurs to emerging Jupiter‑family comets.
highlights: Gemini North telescope captured coma formation around 450P between 2019‑2024.
JWST detected carbon‑dioxide gas but no water vapor in the cometary coma.
Close 1992 encounter with Saturn shortened the orbit, bringing perihelion to 5.4 AU.
Crystalline ice signatures suggest thermal processing of primitive outer‑solar‑system material.
Study accepted by Planetary Science Journal and posted on arXiv.

wrinkled_carbon_nitride_photocatalyst.headline: Wrinkled Graphitic Carbon Nitride Upends Flat‑Sheet Photocatalyst Models
wrinkled_carbon_nitride_photocatalyst.summary: New ARC COE‑CSI study shows g‑C₃N₄ layers buckle and shift, overturning the long‑standing flat‑sheet assumption that guided photocatalytic predictions.
highlights: Computational models revealed a lower‑energy buckled structure for g‑C₃N₄ sheets.
X‑ray scattering experiments confirmed the predicted ripples and lateral shifts between layers.
Doping simulations with phosphorus or nickel showed markedly different effects when the wrinkled geometry was used.
The work appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Materials Advances (2026).

dark_matter_signal_2026_09_04.headline: LUX‑ZEPLIN Detector Records Unexplained High‑Energy Event Hinting at Dark Matter
dark_matter_signal_2026_09_04.summary: The LZ experiment observed a single, anomalous particle interaction in 220 live days that resists explanation as known background, sparking cautious excitement.
highlights: A lone event with 2.6‑sigma significance appears in the low‑background region expected for WIMPs
The interaction suggests a possible WIMP mass of at least 200 GeV/c²
The data were collected underground at SURF using 10 tonnes of liquid xenon

seafood_reverse_aging_mice.headline: Sea Squirrel Plasmalogen Supplement Reverses Aging Signs in Mice
seafood_reverse_aging_mice.summary: Dietary plasmalogen from edible sea squirts improved memory, restored brain synapses, reduced inflammation, and regrew darker hair in aged mice.
highlights: Plasmalogen-fed mice reached the Morris water maze platform significantly faster than controls.
Treated mice showed increased synapse numbers and better synaptic integrity.
Brain inflammation was markedly lower in the plasmalogen group.
Aged mice developed thicker, glossier black hair after supplementation.

infant_sun_formation_dust.headline: Ancient Meteorite Dust Reveals Magnetism Shaped Infant Sun’s Birth
infant_sun_formation_dust.summary: Analysis of calcium‑aluminum‑rich inclusions in the 2008 Antarctic meteorite DOM 08006 shows a magnetic field twelve times Earth’s strength during the solar nebula phase.
highlights: CAIs from DOM 08006 retain remanent magnetization indicating a 12‑fold stronger magnetic field than Earth’s.
Magnetic fields likely assisted gravity in flattening the solar nebula into a protoplanetary disk.
The study, published in PNAS on Aug 7, provides the earliest direct evidence of magnetism before the Sun ignited.

mit_bacteria_transistors.headline: MIT Engineers Bacteria as Living Transistors for Plant‑Based Biological Computers
mit_bacteria_transistors.summary: MIT researchers have engineered Pantoea agglomerans cells to act as transistor‑like components, enabling modular living circuits that can perform logic operations and guide chemical signals.
highlights: Two engineered bacterial transistors switch on or off in response to the signaling molecule OC 6
Three relay strains convert output OHC 14 into inputs for downstream transistors
A 24‑colony circuit demonstrated addition of two inputs, taking about eight hours per calculation

mars_deep_heat.headline: Mars Southern Hemisphere Hotter Than Expected Deep Underground, Caltech Finds
mars_deep_heat.summary: Caltech researchers using tidal tomography of spacecraft gravity data discovered a deep thermal anomaly making Mars’ southern interior 200‑400 °C hotter than models predict.
highlights: Thermal anomaly raises temperatures by 200‑400 °C (290‑750 °F) in the southern mantle
Study combines data from Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Odyssey, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Researchers Alexander Berne and Amirhossein Bagheri published peer‑reviewed results in Nature

dying_radio_galaxies_fade_faster.headline: Young Remnant Radio Galaxies Fade Faster Than Expected, Study Finds
dying_radio_galaxies_fade_faster.summary: Astronomers identified 12 faint remnant radio galaxies aged 8–42 million years, showing that these post‑jet systems disappear much quicker than previously thought.
highlights: Spectral ages range from 8 to 42 million years, with a median of ~12 million years
Higher‑redshift remnants fade more rapidly due to enhanced cosmic‑microwave‑background losses
Multi‑frequency data from MeerKAT, uGMRT, LOFAR, GMRT and the VLA were essential for classification

hidden_order_metasurface_design.headline: Hidden Order in Disordered Metasurfaces Accelerates Nanodevice Design
hidden_order_metasurface_design.summary: Researchers at POSTECH uncovered a repeating Moiré pattern in seemingly aperiodic metasurfaces, enabling rapid analysis of devices containing over a billion nanostructures.
highlights: Discovery of hidden periodicity within complex metasurfaces
Reduction of simulation workload to a few‑dozen nanostructures
Experimental validation of predicted light steering in fabricated devices

ancient_dna_american_cheetah_reassessmen.headline: Ancient DNA Shows Extinct American “Cheetah” Was Arctic‑Adapted Puma Relative
ancient_dna_american_cheetah_reassessmen.summary: Researchers sequenced high‑coverage genomes from Yukon fossils, revealing Miracinonyx trumani was a puma‑like predator that ate fish and thrived far north.
